source_refs.note: Exercise 11.1, Question 4: book page 290 (Q1-Q8). The book prints no answers for Unit 11; every answer here is ours.

blocks.prompt: 4. Create a 3D vector function for a drone flying upward in a spiral.
blocks.explanation:
Yeh 3D mein construction ka open sawal hai, bilkul kitab ke drone wale Example 2 (11.1.3) jaisa.
Spiral mein oopar jana do harkaton ka mel hai: oopar se dekhein to circle mein ghoomna, aur saath saath barabar raftaar se oopar uthna.
Rule: \(x, y\) wahi jo Question 2 mein the, aur oonchai \(z = ct\).
Plan: components, vector form, domain; aakhir mein check ke zameen par us ka saaya (shadow) circle hai.
steps:
Diya gaya: ek drone spiral (ghoomti seerhi jaisa raasta) mein oopar ja raha hai.
Maloom karna: us ki position ke liye 3D vector function \(\mathbf{r}(t)\).
Tareeqa: 11.1.3 ke teen steps. Oopar se dekhein to drone radius \(a\) ke circle par \(\omega\) angular speed se ghoomta hai; saath hi zameen se \(c\) m/s ki steady raftaar se oopar uthta hai.

Step-1: Components maloom karein
\[x(t) = a\cos(\omega t)\]
\[y(t) = a\sin(\omega t)\]
\[z(t) = ct\]
Kyun: \(x\) aur \(y\) bilkul Question 2 ki tarah circle banate hain. Oonchai \(=\) chadhne ki speed \(\times\) waqt, is liye \(z = ct\). Teeno kaam ek saath ho rahe hain, is liye teeno components ek hi \(t\) par depend karte hain.

Step-2: Vector form mein jorein
\[\mathbf{r}(t) = a\cos(\omega t)\,\hat{i} + a\sin(\omega t)\,\hat{j}\]
\[\quad + ct\,\hat{k}\]
Kyun: teesra (vertical) component \(\hat{k}\) ke saath likha jata hai. 3D mein teen unit vectors \(\hat{i}, \hat{j}, \hat{k}\) hote hain.
Is shakal ko helix kehte hain; screw (pech) ki choori bhi isi tarah ghoomti hui oopar jati hai.

Step-3: Domain batayein
\[t \ge 0\]
Kyun: \(t\) udaan ka waqt hai. Teeno components har real \(t\) par defined hain, is liye sirf waqt wali pabandi hai.
Agar drone pehle se kisi oonchai \(h\) par ho to \(z(t) = h + ct\) likhenge.

Ek khaas misaal: radius 4 m, har 8 s mein ek chakkar, 1 m/s se oopar
\[\omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{8} = \dfrac{\pi}{4} \text{ rad/s}\]
\[\mathbf{r}(t) = 4\cos\tfrac{\pi t}{4}\,\hat{i} + 4\sin\tfrac{\pi t}{4}\,\hat{j}\]
\[\quad + t\,\hat{k}\]
\(t = 0, 2, 4, 8\) par drone \((4, 0, 0), (0, 4, 2), (-4, 0, 4), (4, 0, 8)\) par hai.
Kyun: ek chakkar \(2\pi\) radian ka hai aur 8 s mein poora hota hai, is liye \(\omega = 2\pi/8\). Kitab ka Example 2, \(\mathbf{r}(t) = 5\cos t\,\hat{i} + 5\sin t\,\hat{j} + 0.5t\,\hat{k}\), bhi isi qism ka spiral hai.
Dhyan dein: \(\cos\frac{\pi t}{4}\) mein \(t = 2\) rakhein to \(\cos\frac{\pi}{2} = 0\) aata hai, \(\cos 2\) nahin.

Tasdeeq
\[x^2 + y^2 = 16\left(\cos^2\tfrac{\pi t}{4} + \sin^2\tfrac{\pi t}{4}\right)\]
\[= 16 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: oopar se dekhein to drone hamesha radius 4 ke circle par hai, aur \(z = t\) barhta ja raha hai: yahi spiral (helix) hai. Ek chakkar (\(t = 8\)) ke baad drone apni shuru wali jagah ke theek oopar, 8 m oonchai par hai.
Yaad rahe: \(x^2 + y^2\) constant hona circle ki pehchan hai, aur \(z\) ka barhna seerhi ki tarah oopar jana.
blocks.final_answer: \(\mathbf{r}(t) = a\cos(\omega t)\,\hat{i} + a\sin(\omega t)\,\hat{j} + ct\,\hat{k},\ t \ge 0\); misaal: \(\mathbf{r}(t) = 4\cos\frac{\pi t}{4}\,\hat{i} + 4\sin\frac{\pi t}{4}\,\hat{j} + t\,\hat{k}\).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Kitab mein Exercise 11.1 ke jawab chhape hue nahin hain (balke poore Unit 11 ke nahin hain). Is page ka har jawab hamara apna hai: qadam ba qadam hal kiya gaya, computer algebra system (sympy) se alag se check kiya gaya, aur ek solution book se bhi milaya gaya. Aap apna kaam yahan wale hal se mila kar dekh sakte hain. Yeh sawal "open" hai: is ke bahut se sahi jawab ho sakte hain. Hamara jawab ek model jawab hai jo kitab ke teen steps (11.1.3) se banaya gaya hai; agar aap ka function motion ko sahi tarah describe karta hai to woh bhi bilkul sahi hai.
